notes: Background: mid-market collaboration SaaS (team docs, meeting notes, contextual search). Building a chat + summarization assistant embedded in product.
Currently on NimbusAPI for generation and embeddings; exploring move to Redwood Hosted for parity and later Dedicated for predictable throughput and cost.
Primary drivers: reduce per-token costs, improve p95 latency for in-product chat, get stronger SLA and VPC for enterprise customers.
Architecture constraints: existing abstraction layer expects OpenAI-compatible REST (few param names differ). Want minimal code changes on migration (adapter compatibility important).

Performance targets: p95 latency <200ms for short chat turns (<=256 tokens), sustained peak throughput ~20 req/s for server-to-server summarization batch jobs, embeddings throughput ~500 req/hr during nightly jobs.
Cost sensitivity: target 25-40% total token cost reduction vs Nimbus at current usage patterns. Interested in Redwood Optimize suggestions (quantization, batching).
Security & compliance: must support SSO (SAML), SOC2 attestation, KMS integration for key management, audit logs for token-level access, and data residency in us-east for a subset of customers.
POC plan (agreed on 2025-02-12):
- Week 1: Hosted API onboarding + run compatibility adapter to translate our OpenAI-like calls to Redwood endpoints. Capture delta in param mapping.
- Week 2: Run automated prompt parity suite (200 prompts across summarization, Q/A, chat flows) and collect BLEU/ROUGE + human pass/fail. Track regressions per prompt.
- Success criteria: <=3% user-visible regressions on core flows and average token cost reduction >=20% OR p95 latency improvement >=15%.
Notes from call 2025-01-22 (Jordan/Kim intro): 'We need minimal dev lift — if adapters can be a one-line config tweak, we move fast.' AE paraphrase.

Initial Redwood evaluation results (internal dev run 2025-02-05): token cost estimate down ~30% using Redwood's batching + cache suggestions, but three summarization prompts produced shorter answers (quality regression) — flagged for model variant and prompt tuning.

SE notes (Priya): recommended fallback policy = route high-importance customers to a higher-capacity model variant and enable canary rollouts; suggested use of automatic regression alerts tied to parity test set.
Commercial: asked for Dedicated pricing for 3x A100 reserved pool and burst capacity; finance wants transparent unit economics and migration credits for onboarding.
Integration: drive link to adapter prototype in our repo, awaiting Redwood sample compatibility layer (SE to share code snippets).
Open technical questions: how Redwood handles KV cache eviction across model versions; specifics of per-route traceability in Console for audit requests.
Risks called out: prompt regressions during model switch could affect enterprise customers; need staged rollout + rollback path.
Internal next steps (Ambergrove): enable feature-flagged POC in staging, run 2000 prompt/perf synthetic load, assign owners for regressions.

Next steps with Redwood: deliver Hosted POC results by 2025-03-05, schedule Dedicated scoping call (hardware and SLA) w/infra on 2025-02-25, finalize pricing deck with potential 6-month commit options.
